question: Where does PRIMAL's native inertialization time constant (omega = 10 /s) sit on PRIMAL's own boundary-smoothness / motion-quality curve; together with the ARDY part this decides whether inertialization is a generic smoother or a PRIMAL-tuned component
scenes: The 57 jobs of develop_logs/test_runs/20261024_primal_matrix (12 initial states: adapted stand, 5 short and 6 long model-generated histories; seeds 20-24), 600 frames at 30 fps, paused clock
conditions: ground snap and keypoint reprojection on (native defaults); inertialization omega in {2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40} /s and inertialization off; all six conditions in one worker per scene with common random numbers (torch / numpy reseeded per condition) and shuffled execution order
intervention: primal.models.motion_diffuser.inertialize replaced by the native function with the swept omega (dt = 1/30 unchanged); omega 10 runs the unpatched native function
cluster_unit: initial state (G = 12); seeds are paired repetitions

endpoints.primary_descriptive: boundary jerk RMS at the native commit points (frames 14, 28, ...) per omega, paired against inertialization off and against omega 10
secondary: foot sliding given 5 cm contact at 10 cm/s

reading.near_optimal: omega 10 is near-optimal for PRIMAL when its boundary jerk is within 10% of the lowest boundary jerk over the sweep and its common-step jerk is within 10% of the lowest common-step jerk
reading.combined_V3: tuned when the ARDY part reads 'tuned' or omega 10 is not near-optimal for PRIMAL; generic when the ARDY part reads 'generic' and omega 10 is near-optimal for PRIMAL

pilot.admission: Six conditions recorded; finite motion; omega 10 bit-identical to ground1_reproject1_inertialize1 of the same 20261024 matrix job; swept calls equal native inertialization calls for omega != 10; inertialization off has zero inertialization calls; time within 3x estimate

inference.primary: Equal-weight initial-state means of paired differences; cluster t interval with G-1 degrees of freedom and exact sign-flip p

conventions_not_derived.near_optimal_tolerance: 10%, same tolerance as the ARDY V3 stop rule
